title: JVM Structure: Three Generations of the Heap
concept: For efficient cleanup, the JVM divides the Heap into three zones based on object age.

steps.title: main Method Starts
steps.explanation:
**`public static void main(String[] args)`**

The program's entry point.

steps.title: Young Generation
steps.explanation:
Most objects die shortly after creation.
For these short-lived objects, the **Eden** zone and **Survivor** zone are provided.
Cleanup happening here is called Minor GC.

steps.title: Old Generation
steps.explanation:
Objects that survive for a long time in the Young zone (enduring multiple GC cycles) are moved to the **Old** zone (Promotion).
This zone is cleaned less frequently, but when it is, it takes much longer (Major GC).

quiz.question: What is the name of the zone where newly created objects are first allocated?
quiz.explanation: New objects are allocated in the Eden zone, named after the 'Garden of Eden' -- the place of origin.

misconceptions.wrong: All Heap cleanup operations take the same amount of time.
misconceptions.correct: No! The Young zone is small and fast to clean, but the Old zone is large and causes longer program pauses during cleanup.
misconceptions.why: The Old zone has more objects and more complex reference relationships.

keyTakeaway: The JVM manages memory efficiently based on the Weak Generational Hypothesis.
